value.rationale: The fourth Euclidean distance moment is the first nonlinear even chord moment beyond squared distance and detects orientation through covariance cross-terms. Its complete exact amplification range on the canonical two-generator convex-polygon family is nontrivial: only squares maximize, elongated bodies approach the opposite sharp endpoint, and an unexpected algebraic aspect-ratio transition produces an entire angle-invariant slice. These are geometrically motivated exact invariants and equality structures, useful as benchmarks for quantitative refinements of boundary/interior convex-order comparisons; no universal convex-body extension is asserted.
